correctness.rationale: Angular spacings have constant Dirichlet density on ΣΔ_i=2π and have the regular polygon as isolated maximum of each observable; nonregular large gaps are excluded. For x_i=Δ_i−2π/n, Σx_i=0, local deficit aΣx_i²+bΣx_i³+c4Σx_i⁴+O_n(||x||⁵), a=sin(t)/4>0, with b,c4 explicit per observable. The analytic radial implicit solution exists uniformly; parity u↦−u cancels odd ε^(1/2) powers after sphere averaging. Sphere moment contractions ES4=3(n−1)/(n(n+1)) and E(S3²)=6(n−2)/(n(n+1)(n+3)) yield the two B_X formulas. The hyperplane Jacobian 1/√n and Dirichlet density give the C_X normalizations. At n=3 independent exact-sine radial quadrature gave P tail 0.008497355082256 vs two-term 0.008497339004332 at ε=.02 (relative ~1.89e-6) and area tail .006386726321017 vs .006386617312395 at ε=.015 (~1.71e-5). These two finite cases corroborate, but analytic parity/localization prove all fixed n.

final_claim: For each fixed n≥3 uniform points on a unit circle, both near-regular inscribed-polygon area and perimeter endpoint tails have known leading C_X ε^{(n−1)/2} times 1+B_X ε+O_n(ε²), with explicit strictly positive B_X and distinct n³ asymptotics.
limitations: Fixed integer n≥3 and ε↓0, with no n-uniform expansion or U-max second-order claim.
